findings.reason: the author must decide the resources.py verdict and pin the expected set, or the AST inventory test cannot be written as a deterministic assertion.
findings.text: §9's completion instrument asserts the inventory reports "the promoted primitive in reckon/_store.py plus the directory rename in reckon/resources.py if its staged-source rule reaches it"; the conditional makes the expected set undecidable, and §9's own text already fixes reckon/resources.py:1117 `os.replace(staging / relative, destination)` as "the one site that is not a file write", where `staging` is bound from `tempfile.mkdtemp` and the source is a `/` join on that name rather than on a `.parent`, so the stated rule does not reach it

findings.reason: the stated purpose is to end the divergence between the acceptance floor and the dimension set, and a stale "five dimensions" comment on the repaired constant (plus two in the promotion summary) re-introduces the same drift the repair removes.
findings.text: §7 derives REVIEW_ACCEPTANCE_FLOOR from `len(REVIEW_DIMENSIONS)` at reckon/crew/recovery.py:3844 but leaves the count's prose copies in place: reckon/crew/recovery.py:3841 says "five dimensions" two lines above the repaired constant, and reckon/crew/promotion.py:5158 and :8319 both spell "five dimensions" in the promotion summary, while §7's done-when greps only `REVIEW_MAX_SCORE` and therefore cannot see any of them

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — promoting reckon/_store.py:419 to one public `write_atomically(path, render, *, binary=False, ...)` hides temporary naming, unique-suffix creation, fsync, exact mode, directory fsync and binary mode behind a single render callback, and §9 routes ~17 call sites through it; §7 is a one-expression change and adds no module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §9's inventory leaves the reckon/resources.py:1117 verdict conditional while calling it a retained exception, and §7 leaves the dimension count's prose copies at recovery.py:3841 and promotion.py:5158/8319 unaddressed; the owner is named (reckon/_store.py primitive; reckon/crew/review.py REVIEW_DIMENSIONS) but the duplicate's disposition is not.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1474, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §8 names its single addition (`write_atomically`, +1 public_definitions) and states the retired forks are underscore-private and uncounted; §9 names its single addition (the ported inventory rule on reckon/interface_counts.py, +1 public_definitions) with the same reason; neither section adds a CLI option, MCP view or refusal family, and §7 adds nothing to any family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every mechanism the plan extends is cited and verified in code: the census call predicate `primitive_concepts` at docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/code-depth/census.py:233 (nested under the JSON-encoding branch exactly as §9 states, firing only when the function also calls json.dump/dumps), the write primitive `_write_through_sibling_temporary` at reckon/_store.py:419, the module reader `read_trees`/`definitions` at reckon/interface_counts.py, and the dimension tuple `REVIEW_DIMENSIONS` at reckon/crew/review.py:88; §9's rejection of `clones.functions_in` is correct — it returns `_Function` token windows and holds no call node.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §8 keeps `write_json_atomically` (reckon/_store.py:463) as the sole JSON serialiser and adds a `binary` keyword to the generic primitive so the byte publishers in serve.py (503, 567) and the ledger rebuild (ledger.py:1037) migrate rather than fork a second writer; the reason each cannot be merged is stated in the section.
